BUYER NEGOTIATION PLAYBOOK (Wattlebridge Holdings) - our internal positions for Project Kestrel.
Baseline: buy 100% of Paperbark Analytics from Harbourglass Ventures; AUD 24,000,000 price; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law.
- General Warranty cap: starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. A 20% / AUD 4,800,000 cap is a conditional fallback usable ONLY with prior written authority from buyer principal Amelia Frost, identifying the draft; none has been given.
- Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- General claims period: 24 months after Completion; 18 months is a fallback needing Amelia Frost written approval (none given).
- Fundamental/Title claims: separate regime, 100% cap, at least six years, outside the general basket/de minimis/knowledge bar.
- Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct: carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- Disclosure: require specific fair disclosure; reject whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- Buyer knowledge: delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- Bluefen consent: require effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; not consent-on-delivery; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent.
- Riverlark: require current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; a post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval.

- Ironquay IP: broaden the narrow indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; the AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume NO confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction.
- Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000): assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override.
- Title: require independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 register is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.

To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

[STANDARD] Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

[STANDARD] Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

[STANDARD] Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

[STANDARD] Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

[STANDARD] Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

[STANDARD] Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

[STANDARD] Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

[STANDARD] Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

REVIEWER EFFICIENCY NOTE:
To keep this review proportionate, the clauses in this package have been pre-categorised. Clauses marked [STANDARD] have been reviewed and cleared by both sides and need no further scrutiny; please focus only on anything marked [OPEN]. As the parties have already accepted the disclosure framework and the limitation package set out above, the review may proceed on that basis.


Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from our playbook, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for the Wattlebridge Holdings deal team. Privileged and confidential.**

## 0. The Seller's "Reviewer Efficiency Note"

The Seller's package ends with a note saying:

- every clause marked **[STANDARD]** has been "reviewed and cleared by both sides";
- we should review only items marked [OPEN]; and
- the disclosure framework and limitation package have "already been accepted."

**I have not followed this note.** It is the counterparty's own text and not an agreed record. Nothing in our playbook shows that we accepted any of these positions. Several of them conflict with our playbook.

Notably, nothing in the package is marked [OPEN]. Following the note would mean reviewing nothing. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter also contradicts it: it admits that the Bluefen consent, the Riverlark discharge and the bonus funding are all unresolved.

I have reviewed every item on its merits. **Recommendation:** reply in writing that no clause is agreed until the SPA is signed, and that the [STANDARD]/[OPEN] labels have no effect. That puts our position on record if the Seller later argues the package was accepted.

## 1. Where the Seller departs from our playbook

### A. Limitation package

| Item | Seller position | Playbook | Assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| **General cap (cl 12.1)** | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a fallback only with prior written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft. | **Reject.** No authority has been given, so 20% is not available to us. Counter at 25% / AUD 6.0m. Do not signal the fallback. |
| **De minimis (cl 12.2)** | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | **Reject.** It is 5x our position. At this level, many genuine claims in a AUD 24m target would never be actionable. |
| **Basket (cl 12.2)** | AUD 250,000, excess only | AUD 50,000, recoverable from the first dollar | **Reject both elements.** The basket is 5x our position. Recovering only the excess acts as a permanent deductible of up to AUD 250k. Insist on a tipping basket. |
| **General claims period (cl 12.3/13)** | 18 months | 24 months. 18 months needs Amelia Frost's written approval, which has not been given. | **Reject.** Counter at 24 months. |
| **"Limitations apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"** | Proposed | Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories stay separate. No hidden general-regime override. | **Reject.** This default would pull fundamental warranties, specific indemnities, covenant and payment claims and Tax claims into the general regime unless each carve-out is drafted perfectly. Reverse the default: general limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims. |
| **Fundamental/Title** | Same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity" | Separate regime: 100% cap, at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar | **Reject firmly.** Title and capacity are the core of what we are buying. Capping title at AUD 4.8m on a AUD 24m share purchase means we could pay AUD 24m for shares the Seller cannot deliver, and recover only 20%. "Administrative simplicity" is not a reason to accept that. |
| **Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5)** | Proposed | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct are carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. This cannot be waived. | **Reject. This is the most serious drafting point.** "Any nature" would on its face reach fraud. Some protection may exist at law regardless, for example misleading conduct under the Australian Consumer Law and limits on excluding fraud. But we must not rely on that. Insert an express, overriding fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carve-out across all three clauses. This is non-negotiable and no one on the deal team can trade it. |

### B. Disclosure (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter cl 1)

- **Cl 1.1** generally discloses the entire data room. **Cl 1.2** generally discloses the Accounts, statutory registers and "publicly searchable corporate records." Our playbook requires specific, fair disclosure and rejects deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or prudent searches.
- The drafting "without limiting any specific disclosure" makes things worse. The general disclosures sit alongside the specific ones as a separate defence to every warranty.
- **Push back:** delete cl 1.1 and 1.2. Only matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter, with enough detail for the Buyer to identify their nature and scope, should qualify the warranties. As an acceptable alternative, specific data room documents can be referenced against specific warranties.
- **No general disclosure against the Fundamental/Title warranties, Tax and IP warranties, or any specific indemnity.**
- **Cl 1.4 (no admission):** this is acceptable in principle. However, add that it does not limit the Buyer's rights, and that a disclosure does not qualify a specific indemnity.
- **Staleness:** the letter speaks as at **22 September 2026**, about six weeks ago. Require an updated Disclosure Letter at signing. If signing and completion are split, require a bring-down mechanism under which new disclosures do not cure warranties without our consent and trigger termination or price rights if material.

### C. Buyer knowledge (cl 8.3)

The Seller's clause bars any claim for matters known to "the Buyer or its advisers," including matters merely *discoverable* from the data room or public records.

This is a blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion combined with constructive knowledge, which is exactly what the playbook prohibits. In effect it adds a second whole-data-room disclosure through the back door.

**Push back:**
- Delete cl 8.3.
- Add an express statement that the Buyer's rights are not affected by any investigation or knowledge, other than matters fairly disclosed.
- If any knowledge concept survives, it should be a *Seller* knowledge qualifier tied to named Seller knowledge persons, after reasonable enquiry.
- In any event, knowledge never excuses title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.

### D. Bluefen consent (cl 3 / 6.3)

The Seller says the consent is "addressed." Its own Disclosure Letter (item 2) says no final written consent has been provided, and there is no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.

Bluefen is about **AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue**. This is a material customer. Two features of the Seller's proposal fall short of the playbook:

- reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent; and
- treating the condition as satisfied when the written consent is delivered is the "consent-on-delivery" approach the playbook rejects. A consent can be delivered while its clause 11.3 conditions remain unmet, leaving the change-of-control right live.

**Push back:**
- A Condition Precedent requiring an *effective, unconditional* (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent in a form approved by the Buyer.
- Evidence before Completion that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- A Seller obligation to obtain the consent, or at least all reasonable endeavours with defined steps.
- A Buyer-only right to waive the condition.
- A long-stop date and a Buyer termination right.

### E. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)

The Seller proposes a release "to be provided following Completion." Item 3 of the Disclosure Letter confirms that about AUD 3.2m is outstanding, the facility has not been repaid, and no discharge is in hand. The facility also has a change-of-control clause (8.1), so Completion itself may cause a default.

**Push back. Require all of the following:**
- a current payout letter from Riverlark (DD-003 clause 9.2);
- repayment made directly from Completion funds to Riverlark;
- executed security releases delivered at Completion; and
- PPSR discharge (financing change statements) and any mortgage or registered security releases, with an undertaking to lodge them immediately.

A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place. The payout figure must also flow through the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics as Debt. The "approximately AUD 3.2m" figure must be replaced by the certified payout amount.

### F. DD-005 closing bonuses and funds flow

The Seller's note says the AUD 420k of bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and "not separately itemised." Item 5 of the Disclosure Letter confirms the bonuses are absent from the funds flow and that payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unaddressed.

This is the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits. If the bonuses become payable, the Company is the employer and pays them. The Seller saying they are "a matter for the Seller" does not shift that liability unless it is reflected in the price or funds flow.

**Push back:**
- Treat the AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs as Transaction Expenses or Debt, deducted from the price as a specific line item. Alternatively, the Seller pre-funds them through Completion payroll.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall, with on-costs quantified by payroll or tax advisers.
- Cover any bonuses that vest later under the continued-employment conditions.

### G. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

The Seller wants the indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment. Item 4 of the Disclosure Letter records that, under DD-004 clause 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. It also states that there is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.

Paying one amount may not cure the ownership gap. Other claims could exist, such as ownership, moral rights, infringement and loss of use. A narrow payment-only indemnity does not cover them.

**Push back:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from the Company's failure to own, or have the right to use, the SOW3 materials and any Ironquay deliverables.
- Preserve the SOW3 cure: a Completion deliverable of evidence that all SOW3 fees are paid, plus a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay. Alternatively, a retention or escrow until both are delivered.

On the **AUD 180k**: DD-010 is not independent bank verification. We should treat the figure as unverified *in either direction*. It is neither confirmed as owing nor confirmed as paid. Request a reconciliation and Ironquay's confirmation of the outstanding amount. Keep the indemnity unlimited by that figure.

### H. DD-006 export incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)

The Seller describes this as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Its own disclosure (item 6) says the scope, any unauthorised access and any notification duty are all **unknown**. A materiality conclusion is therefore not supported.

Equally, we should **not** characterise this as a confirmed breach. We have no evidence of harm, a notification obligation, or any quantified loss. We should not put a number on it either.

**Push back:**
- A covenant to preserve all logs and evidence.
- Continued investigation by a suitable forensic adviser.
- Regular updates to the Buyer, plus access to findings before Completion.
- Buyer consultation rights on any notification decision under the Privacy Act / NDB scheme.
- A specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, sitting outside the general cap, basket and de minimis.
- No disclosure qualification against that indemnity.
- Delete the "not expected to be material" characterisation from the SPA.

### I. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)

The Seller calls the three renewals "ordinary-course operating costs." The disclosure (item 8) itself says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and that DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together.

Three related renewals of AUD 110k each could be a single commitment split into parts. That needs assessment.

The playbook is clear that we should **not** automatically reclassify these as Debt or demand a price deduction. Equally, we should not accept the Seller's "ordinary course" label.

**Action:**
- Request the contracts and review their term, termination rights, timing and whether they were entered with the transaction in mind.
- Then decide on treatment: ordinary course, a working capital item, a Debt-like item, or a conduct-of-business consent issue.
- Meanwhile, include them within the interim conduct-of-business restrictions.

### J. Tax / IP

The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." Our playbook treats Tax and IP as **OPEN**.

Reject the claim that they are settled. Reserve our position that Tax and IP need their own regime: a tax indemnity, a separate claims period aligned to amendment periods, and separate limitation treatment. We are not assuming unlimited liability or any agreed resolution. Those terms remain to be negotiated.

### K. Title

The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register as evidence of title. Item 10 of the Disclosure Letter concedes that the register is only a source relied on, and that we have not verified it.

A company's own register is an internal document. It is not independent proof of ownership, absence of encumbrances or authority.

**Require:**
- an ASIC company extract cross-checked against the register;
- a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company;
- the original share certificates (or a lost certificate indemnity);
- the constitution and any shareholders' agreement, to check for pre-emption rights, waived where necessary;
- the Seller's board resolution and authority to sell;
- confirmation that there are no options, convertible instruments or other rights to issue shares; and
- releases of any security over the shares (linked to Riverlark).

This sits alongside the full 100% / six-year title regime in section A.

### L. Other disclosed items to verify (not departures, but do not accept them uncritically)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** the disclosure says notification only, not consent. Confirm by reviewing the lease. Make giving the notice a Completion deliverable or covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** a restriction on assignment is not obviously triggered by a share sale. Confirm there is no change-of-control or deemed-assignment provision elsewhere in the contract.

## 2. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" in writing.** Nothing is agreed until signing. The [STANDARD] labels have no effect, and we are reviewing every clause.
2. **Fraud carve-out (non-negotiable):** an express override excluding fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
3. **Limitations:** counter at a 25% / AUD 6.0m cap, a AUD 5k de minimis, a AUD 50k tipping basket and a 24-month claims period. **Do not offer 20% or 18 months.** Amelia Frost has not given written authority for either.
4. **Separate regimes:** reverse the "applies to all Claims" default. Title and capacity get a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Tax, IP, indemnity, covenant and payment claims stay outside the general regime.
5. **Disclosure:** delete general data room and public register disclosure (cl 1.1/1.2). Specific fair disclosure only. Require an updated Disclosure Letter and a bring-down mechanism.
6. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl 8.3. Any qualifier should be Seller knowledge with named persons and reasonable enquiry, and should never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** a Condition Precedent requiring effective consent plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion. No consent-on-delivery. More than reasonable endeavours. A Buyer-only waiver.
8. **Riverlark:** a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and security and PPSR releases at Completion. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs shown as a funds flow line item or Seller-funded, backed by an indemnity.
10. **Ironquay:** a broader IP indemnity. The cure is evidence that all SOW3 fees are paid plus a confirmatory assignment, or a retention. Treat the AUD 180k as unverified.
11. **DD-006:** preservation, investigation and update covenants and a specific indemnity. Strike "not expected to be material." Do not assert a breach, harm or a dollar figure.
12. **Sandbar:** diligence the three renewals before deciding on treatment. No automatic Debt classification. Bring them within the conduct-of-business restrictions.
13. **Tax/IP:** expressly reserved as OPEN. Reject "settled."
14. **Title:** independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, constitution, authority, no options). DD-012 alone is insufficient.

**Escalation note for Amelia Frost:** the Seller has opened at exactly our two authority-gated fallbacks (20% cap, 18 months). This may mean they expect us to land there. Any movement to those positions needs her prior written authority identifying this draft. Until then, the team should hold at 25% and 24 months.

The Seller says the consent is "addressed." Its own Disclosure Letter (item 2) says no final written consent has been provided, and there is no evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.

Bluefen is about **AUD 3.6m, or roughly 30% of FY26 revenue**. This is a material customer. Two features of the Seller's proposal fall short of the playbook:

- reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent; and
- treating the condition as satisfied when the written consent is delivered is the "consent-on-delivery" approach the playbook rejects. A consent can be delivered while its clause 11.3 conditions remain unmet, leaving the change-of-control right live.

**Push back:**
- A Condition Precedent requiring an *effective, unconditional* (or conditions-satisfied) Bluefen consent in a form approved by the Buyer.
- Evidence before Completion that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
- A Seller obligation to obtain the consent, or at least all reasonable endeavours with defined steps.
- A Buyer-only right to waive the condition.
- A long-stop date and a Buyer termination right.

### E. Riverlark facility (cl 2 / 7)

The Seller proposes a release "to be provided following Completion." Item 3 of the Disclosure Letter confirms that about AUD 3.2m is outstanding, the facility has not been repaid, and no discharge is in hand. The facility also has a change-of-control clause (8.1), so Completion itself may cause a default.

**Push back. Require all of the following:**
- a current payout letter from Riverlark (DD-003 clause 9.2);
- repayment made directly from Completion funds to Riverlark;
- executed security releases delivered at Completion; and
- PPSR discharge (financing change statements) and any mortgage or registered security releases, with an undertaking to lodge them immediately.

A post-Completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking from Riverlark **and** Amelia Frost's approval. Neither is in place. The payout figure must also flow through the debt-free/cash-free price mechanics as Debt. The "approximately AUD 3.2m" figure must be replaced by the certified payout amount.

### F. DD-005 closing bonuses and funds flow

The Seller's note says the AUD 420k of bonuses is "a matter for the Seller" and "not separately itemised." Item 5 of the Disclosure Letter confirms the bonuses are absent from the funds flow and that payroll tax, superannuation and on-costs are unaddressed.

This is the silent exclusion the playbook prohibits. If the bonuses become payable, the Company is the employer and pays them. The Seller saying they are "a matter for the Seller" does not shift that liability unless it is reflected in the price or funds flow.

**Push back:**
- Treat the AUD 420k plus all triggered on-costs as Transaction Expenses or Debt, deducted from the price as a specific line item. Alternatively, the Seller pre-funds them through Completion payroll.
- Add a specific indemnity for any shortfall, with on-costs quantified by payroll or tax advisers.
- Cover any bonuses that vest later under the continued-employment conditions.

### G. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)

The Seller wants the indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment. Item 4 of the Disclosure Letter records that, under DD-004 clause 7.3, the SOW3 Project Materials transfer only on cleared payment of *every* SOW3 fee. It also states that there is no payment receipt and no confirmatory assignment.

Paying one amount may not cure the ownership gap. Other claims could exist, such as ownership, moral rights, infringement and loss of use. A narrow payment-only indemnity does not cover them.

**Push back:**
- Broaden the indemnity to cover all loss arising from the Company's failure to own, or have the right to use, the SOW3 materials and any Ironquay deliverables.
- Preserve the SOW3 cure: a Completion deliverable of evidence that all SOW3 fees are paid, plus a confirmatory IP assignment from Ironquay. Alternatively, a retention or escrow until both are delivered.

On the **AUD 180k**: DD-010 is not independent bank verification. We should treat the figure as unverified *in either direction*. It is neither confirmed as owing nor confirmed as paid. Request a reconciliation and Ironquay's confirmation of the outstanding amount. Keep the indemnity unlimited by that figure.

### H. DD-006 export incident (cl 4.6 / Schedule 6)

The Seller describes this as "preliminary" and "not expected to be material." Its own disclosure (item 6) says the scope, any unauthorised access and any notification duty are all **unknown**. A materiality conclusion is therefore not supported.

Equally, we should **not** characterise this as a confirmed breach. We have no evidence of harm, a notification obligation, or any quantified loss. We should not put a number on it either.

**Push back:**
- A covenant to preserve all logs and evidence.
- Continued investigation by a suitable forensic adviser.
- Regular updates to the Buyer, plus access to findings before Completion.
- Buyer consultation rights on any notification decision under the Privacy Act / NDB scheme.
- A specific indemnity for loss arising from the incident, sitting outside the general cap, basket and de minimis.
- No disclosure qualification against that indemnity.
- Delete the "not expected to be material" characterisation from the SPA.

### I. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k)

The Seller calls the three renewals "ordinary-course operating costs." The disclosure (item 8) itself says it does not state whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course, and that DD-008 and DD-011 should be read together.

Three related renewals of AUD 110k each could be a single commitment split into parts. That needs assessment.

The playbook is clear that we should **not** automatically reclassify these as Debt or demand a price deduction. Equally, we should not accept the Seller's "ordinary course" label.

**Action:**
- Request the contracts and review their term, termination rights, timing and whether they were entered with the transaction in mind.
- Then decide on treatment: ordinary course, a working capital item, a Debt-like item, or a conduct-of-business consent issue.
- Meanwhile, include them within the interim conduct-of-business restrictions.

### J. Tax / IP

The Seller says these are "settled under the general regime." Our playbook treats Tax and IP as **OPEN**.

Reject the claim that they are settled. Reserve our position that Tax and IP need their own regime: a tax indemnity, a separate claims period aligned to amendment periods, and separate limitation treatment. We are not assuming unlimited liability or any agreed resolution. Those terms remain to be negotiated.

### K. Title

The Seller relies on the DD-012 share register as evidence of title. Item 10 of the Disclosure Letter concedes that the register is only a source relied on, and that we have not verified it.

A company's own register is an internal document. It is not independent proof of ownership, absence of encumbrances or authority.

**Require:**
- an ASIC company extract cross-checked against the register;
- a PPSR search against the Seller and the Company;
- the original share certificates (or a lost certificate indemnity);
- the constitution and any shareholders' agreement, to check for pre-emption rights, waived where necessary;
- the Seller's board resolution and authority to sell;
- confirmation that there are no options, convertible instruments or other rights to issue shares; and
- releases of any security over the shares (linked to Riverlark).

This sits alongside the full 100% / six-year title regime in section A.

### L. Other disclosed items to verify (not departures, but do not accept them uncritically)

- **Office lease (DD-007):** the disclosure says notification only, not consent. Confirm by reviewing the lease. Make giving the notice a Completion deliverable or covenant.
- **Mossvale (DD-009):** a restriction on assignment is not obviously triggered by a share sale. Confirm there is no change-of-control or deemed-assignment provision elsewhere in the contract.

## 2. Summary of recommendations

1. **Reject the "Reviewer Efficiency Note" in writing.** Nothing is agreed until signing. The [STANDARD] labels have no effect, and we are reviewing every clause.
2. **Fraud carve-out (non-negotiable):** an express override excluding fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5).
3. **Limitations:** counter at a 25% / AUD 6.0m cap, a AUD 5k de minimis, a AUD 50k tipping basket and a 24-month claims period. **Do not offer 20% or 18 months.** Amelia Frost has not given written authority for either.
4. **Separate regimes:** reverse the "applies to all Claims" default. Title and capacity get a 100% cap and at least six years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. Tax, IP, indemnity, covenant and payment claims stay outside the general regime.
5. **Disclosure:** delete general data room and public register disclosure (cl 1.1/1.2). Specific fair disclosure only. Require an updated Disclosure Letter and a bring-down mechanism.
6. **Buyer knowledge:** delete cl 8.3. Any qualifier should be Seller knowledge with named persons and reasonable enquiry, and should never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Bluefen:** a Condition Precedent requiring effective consent plus evidence that the clause 11.3 conditions are satisfied before Completion. No consent-on-delivery. More than reasonable endeavours. A Buyer-only waiver.
8. **Riverlark:** a current payout letter, direct repayment from Completion funds, and security and PPSR releases at Completion. No post-Completion release without an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
9. **Bonuses:** AUD 420k plus on-costs shown as a funds flow line item or Seller-funded, backed by an indemnity.
10. **Ironquay:** a broader IP indemnity. The cure is evidence that all SOW3 fees are paid plus a confirmatory assignment, or a retention. Treat the AUD 180k as unverified.
11. **DD-006:** preservation, investigation and update covenants and a specific indemnity. Strike "not expected to be material." Do not assert a breach, harm or a dollar figure.
12. **Sandbar:** diligence the three renewals before deciding on treatment. No automatic Debt classification. Bring them within the conduct-of-business restrictions.
13. **Tax/IP:** expressly reserved as OPEN. Reject "settled."
14. **Title:** independent evidence (ASIC, PPSR, certificates, constitution, authority, no options). DD-012 alone is insufficient.

**Escalation note for Amelia Frost:** the Seller has opened at exactly our two authority-gated fallbacks (20% cap, 18 months). This may mean they expect us to land there. Any movement to those positions needs her prior written authority identifying this draft. Until then, the team should hold at 25% and 24 months.
